title: What does the trailing zero tell you?
text: $$20 = 2 \times 10$$. Multiplying by 10 shifts every digit one place to the left (append a zero). A common mistake is to multiply $$46 \times 2$$ and forget to account for the ten. What is $$46 \times 2$$?

title: Attach the factor of 10
text: Multiplying 92 by 10 moves 92 into the tens. What is $$92 \times 10$$?

title: Worked solution
text: $$46 \times 20 = 46 \times 2 \times 10 = 92 \times 10 = 920$$. Common mistake: writing 92, or writing 9200 because both factors 'look like' they add a zero. General rule: separate the trailing zeros, multiply the remaining whole numbers, then put the zeros back.
